\subsection{All finite cyclic outer groups, with their actual automorphism extensions}

\begin{statement}{D.47}{Proved}{Complete peripheral chief fibres for every cyclic outer group}
Let \(S\) be a finite nonabelian simple group for which
\[
 \epsilon:\operatorname{Aut}(S)\longrightarrow
       \operatorname{Out}(S)=C_M
 \tag{D.47.1}
\]
has cyclic target, where \(M\geq1\) is arbitrary.
Identify \(S\) with its inner automorphisms.
Let \(1\to A=S^\Omega\to E\xrightarrow{\pi}D\to1\)
be an actual finite chief extension, and fix an epimorphism
\(q_E:\widehat F(x_1,x_2)\twoheadrightarrow E\).
Write \(x_3=(x_1x_2)^{-1}\),
\(X_i=q_E(x_i)\), \(q_0=\pi q_E\), and \(d_i=q_0(x_i)\).
For every epimorphism \(q_1:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow D\),
every specified \(h_i\in D\) with
\[
                    q_1(x_i)=h_id_ih_i^{-1},
 \tag{D.47.2}
\]
and arbitrary lifts \(H_i\in E\) of these \(h_i\), the finite set
\[
 \mathcal E(q_1;H_i)=
 \left\{f:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow E:
   \pi f=q_1,\quad
   f(x_i)\in\{aH_iX_iH_i^{-1}a^{-1}:a\in A\}
                 \ (1\leq i\leq3)\right\}
 \tag{D.47.3}
\]
has exactly the same positive cardinality as
\(\mathcal E(q_0;1,1,1)\).
This includes the complete ordinary peripheral fibre and every
choice of its prescribed base conjugators.
The actual extension \textup{(D.47.1)} is retained throughout.

Consequently every D.37 automorphism \(\beta_Q\) on every
specified \(P_n\) lifts through every chief extension of this
kind above \(P_n\), with the literal conjugators
\(1,f_Q,h_Q\). Its maximal pro-five quotient is the given
\(P_n\), and the induced map there is \(\beta_Q\).
Any additional prescribed epimorphism to a finite group over
\(D\) with solvable kernel is retained through the actual
fibre product.
\end{statement}

\begin{proof}
We prove the composite-order source maps first, and then give
the exact extension, boundary, subtraction, and generation maps.

\paragraph{Representatives in the actual outer extension.}
Choose an element \(t\in\operatorname{Aut}(S)\) with
\(\epsilon(t)=1\in C_M\). For \(a\in C_M\), choose the
integer representative \(\widetilde a\in\{0,\ldots,M-1\}\),
and put
\[
                  L(a)=t^{\widetilde a},\qquad L(0)=1.
 \tag{D.47.4}
\]
The elements
\(L(a)L(b)L(a+b)^{-1}\) belong to the actual subgroup \(S\).
They remain in all products below. Every change of coordinates
will use a displayed element \(L(a)\) and its actual inverse.
For a subgroup \(H\leq C_M\), write
\(\widetilde S_H=\epsilon^{-1}(H)\).
If \(|H|=m\), its generator \(M/m\) has the actual lift
\(t_H=t^{M/m}\); identify \(H\) with \(C_m\) using that
generator.

\paragraph{The effective phase of a boundary.}
Use the oriented surface presentation of D.45.6, with
\(b\geq2\), and let \(\chi:\Pi\twoheadrightarrow C_m\)
be a surjective character. Write \(j_i=\chi(c_i)\).
An automorphism preserving \(\chi\) and every positive
boundary class has
\(\theta(c_i)=u_ic_iu_i^{-1}\). Its effective phase is
\[
                 [\chi(u_i)]\in C_m/\langle j_i\rangle.
 \tag{D.47.5}
\]
This quotient retains exactly the ambiguity in the based path.
Each boundary is primitive in the free group obtained by
eliminating one other boundary. Its centralizer is its cyclic
subgroup: in a free basis containing that boundary, a reduced
word with a letter outside that cyclic subgroup cannot commute
with the basis letter. Thus two conjugating words differ by
a boundary power, proving \textup{(D.47.5)} is well-defined.
For character-preserving automorphisms the effective phases
add under composition. Under a change of surface coordinates,
transport \(\chi\) with that change; the phases of the change
and its inverse then cancel in these quotients.

The same quotient is exactly what is needed for target
conjugacy sets. For \(a\in\widetilde S_H\) with outer
coordinate \(j\in C_m\), and \(k\in\langle j\rangle\),
choose an integer \(v\) with \(vj=k\) in \(C_m\).
Then \(t_H^ka^{-v}\in S\), and the actual equality
\[
 t_H^k a t_H^{-k}
     =(t_H^ka^{-v})\,a\,(t_H^ka^{-v})^{-1}
 \tag{D.47.6}
\]
shows that every \(S\)-conjugacy invariant subset of that
outer coset is fixed by the phase subgroup \(\langle j\rangle\).
No order relation for \(t_H\) was used.

\paragraph{Every effective phase is realized by source automorphisms.}
For one handle and a boundary \(c\), retain the exact maps
\(P\) and \(T\) on \([a,b]c\):
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P(a)&=c^{-1}ac,&P(b)&=c^{-1}a^{-1}cab c,&
 P(c)&=c^{-1}a^{-1}cac,\\
 T(a)&=a,&T(b)&=ba,&T(c)&=c.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{D.47.7}
\]
Both fix \([a,b]c\) literally. D.45.8--9 give the
explicit Nielsen inverse of \(P\), and \(T^{-1}(b)=ba^{-1}\).
They commute. Moreover \(P\) fixes \((ac)^{-1}\), and its
restriction to \(\langle a,c\rangle\) is conjugation by that
word. Hence for all integers \(N,k\), the map
\(\theta=P^N\circ T^k\) is an actual automorphism, with
inverse \(T^{-k}\circ P^{-N}\), and
\[
 \begin{split}
  \chi(\theta(a))&=\chi(a),\qquad
  \chi(\theta(c))=j,\\
  \chi(\theta(b))&=\chi(b)+Nj+k\chi(a),\\
  \theta(c)&=(ac)^{-N}c(ac)^N.
 \end{split}
 \tag{D.47.8}
\]

Fix a prime power \(\ell^e\Vert m\), and let
\(N\in\mathbf Z\) be a CRT idempotent: it is \(1\) modulo
\(\ell^e\) and \(0\) modulo every other primary factor of \(m\).
If \(\ell\nmid j\), the entire \(\ell\)-primary subgroup
of \(C_m\) lies in \(\langle j\rangle\), so this component
already acts trivially by \textup{(D.47.6)}.
Suppose \(\ell\mid j\). Surjectivity of \(\chi\) supplies
a handle or boundary value which is a unit modulo \(\ell\).

First let a handle supply such a value. If its \(a\)-value
is a unit, put \(a_0=\chi(a)\). If only its \(b\)-value is
a unit, use the exact change \(a\mapsto ab,\ b\mapsto b\)
and its inverse; the new \(a_0\) is \(\chi(a)+\chi(b)\),
which is a unit modulo \(\ell\). In these coordinates choose
\[
 k\equiv-j a_0^{-1}\pmod{\ell^e},\qquad
 k\equiv0\pmod{m/\ell^e}.
 \tag{D.47.9}
\]
Equations \textup{(D.47.8)--(D.47.9)} give
\(Nj+ka_0=0\) in \(C_m\), so \(\theta\) preserves
the entire character. Its phase at \(c\) is
\(-N(a_0+j)\). That phase is a unit at \(\ell\) and is
zero at all other primary factors. Every other boundary is
fixed literally. Powers of \(\theta\) therefore supply
every \(\ell\)-primary effective phase at \(c\).

If a boundary \(d\) supplies the unit, put
\(d_0=\chi(d)\). The exact Hurwitz square of D.45.11--12,
raised to the \(N\)-th power, conjugates \(c\) by \((cd)^N\).
It conjugates \(d\) by \((cd)^Nd^{-N}\). These literal words
give phases
\[
                     N(j+d_0)\quad\hbox{at }c,
                         \qquad Nj\quad\hbox{at }d.
 \tag{D.47.10}
\]
The first is a unit in the required primary component and
zero elsewhere. The second belongs to \(\langle d_0\rangle\):
its other primary components vanish, and \(d_0\) is a unit
in the remaining component. Thus its effective phase at
\(d\) is zero. The map preserves \(\chi\), fixes all other
boundaries, and its powers supply the required component at
\(c\).

The positive boundary swaps and handle-block swaps in
D.45.11 and D.45.13 put any selected boundary and supplier
in these positions. Pull back by their explicit inverses.
The comparison following \textup{(D.47.5)} retains the
effective phases in the original presentation. This proves
surjectivity of the effective-phase map onto
\(\prod_i C_m/\langle j_i\rangle\), using finite
compositions of actual surface automorphisms.

It follows that for arbitrary \(S\)-conjugacy invariant
sets \(T_i\subset\widetilde S_H\) in the specified outer
cosets, independently replacing them by
\(t_H^{k_i}T_it_H^{-k_i}\) preserves the number of
epimorphisms \(\widehat\Pi\twoheadrightarrow\widetilde S_H\)
with outer character \(\chi\) and those boundary conditions.
Indeed precomposition by the constructed automorphism gives
the bijection: its conjugating word has image in
\(S t_H^{k_i}\), up to the harmless subgroup in
\textup{(D.47.6)}. Precomposition by the explicit inverse
reverses the bijection and preserves surjectivity.

\paragraph{Matching composite cyclic characters exactly.}
Two oriented pants covers of the same index, with the matched
boundary cycles below, have the same genus. Choose standard
handle presentations and use the positive boundary swaps to
match their boundary classes. Consider two characters to
\(C_m\) which have the same image \(C_m\) and the same
values \(j_1,\ldots,j_b\) on those matched boundaries.
Define
\[
       d=\gcd(m,\widetilde j_1,\ldots,\widetilde j_b),
       \qquad (j_1,\ldots,j_b)=d(\mathbf Z/m)\subset\mathbf Z/m.
 \tag{D.47.11}
\]
In genus zero the characters already agree. In positive
genus, their handle covectors reduce modulo \(d\) to
primitive covectors. Over each local ring
\(\mathbf Z/\ell^a\) dividing \(d\), elementary symplectic
operations carry a primitive covector to the first basis
covector: place a unit entry in the first symplectic pair,
clear the other entries, and scale that pair by
\(\operatorname{diag}(u,u^{-1})\). The elementary
factorization in D.41 realizes the scaling as well.
All these elementary operations are powers of the actual
handle Dehn twists listed there. Choose their parameters
by CRT to be the required ones in the selected primary
factor and zero in the others. Thus a finite product of
integral surface maps matches the handle covectors modulo
\(d\), while fixing every boundary.

The remaining difference in each handle coordinate lies
in the ideal generated by the \(j_i\) in
\textup{(D.47.11)}. The bounding-pair map for a basis curve
\(a\) and a boundary \(c_i\) acts on homology by
\(v\mapsto v+\langle v,a\rangle c_i\), as in D.45.15.
Its powers change the dual handle-character coordinate by
arbitrary multiples of \(j_i\), and fix all the other
handle coordinates and the boundary values. An integral
linear combination expressing the required difference in
the ideal \((j_1,\ldots,j_b)\) therefore corrects that
coordinate exactly. Doing this for each handle matches
the characters in \(C_m\). These are actual based surface
maps, with inverse maps. Their additional boundary phases
are all removed by \textup{(D.47.5)--(D.47.10)}.
For the trivial image the characters agree without this
correction. This proves the required epimorphism-count
comparison for every cyclic image, including every proper
subgroup of \(C_M\).

\paragraph{The given chief extension and each intermediate embedding.}
Let \(D_*\) be a factor stabilizer and use the right action
\(\Omega=D_*\backslash D\). Centerlessness gives the exact
isomorphism
\[
 E\longrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}(A)
             \mathbin{\times_{\operatorname{Out}(A)}}D,
          \qquad e\longmapsto(\operatorname{Ad}_e,\pi(e)).
 \tag{D.47.12}
\]
Injectivity follows from \(Z(A)=1\); for surjectivity,
choose a lift of the prescribed base element and correct
its automorphism by the unique required inner element of
\(A\).
Write the outer action as the actual cocycle
\(b_d(\omega)\in C_M\), with
\(b_{de}(\omega)=b_d(\omega)+b_e(\omega d)\).
Choose \(t_\omega\in D\), \(t_{\omega_0}=1\), and put
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \epsilon_*(c)&=b_c(\omega_0)\quad(c\in D_*),&
 s_\omega&=b_{t_\omega}(\omega_0),\\
 k(\omega,d)&=t_\omega d t_{\omega d}^{-1},&
 b_d(\omega)&=-s_\omega+\epsilon_*(k(\omega,d))+s_{\omega d}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{D.47.13}
\]
The actual gauge
\((z,d)\mapsto(L(s_\omega)z(\omega)L(s_{\omega d})^{-1},d)\)
carries \(E\), and every specified \(X_i,H_i\), to
\[
 E_*=
 \{(z,d)\in\operatorname{Aut}(S)^\Omega\rtimes D:
             \epsilon(z(\omega))=\epsilon_*(k(\omega,d))\},
 \qquad
 (z,d)(w,e)=(z(\omega)w(\omega d),de).
 \tag{D.47.14}
\]
For multiplication, the adjacent factors
\(L(s_{\omega d})^{-1}L(s_{\omega d})\) cancel literally.
This proves the map and its inverse using the actual
representatives \textup{(D.47.4)}.

For each \(D_*\leq C\leq D\), retain every character
\(\epsilon_C:C\to C_M\) extending \(\epsilon_*\).
Choose \(R_\nu\) representing \(C\backslash D\), with
\(R_C=1\). Define
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 k_C(\nu,d)&=R_\nu dR_{\nu d}^{-1},&
 b_C(d,\nu)&=\epsilon_C(k_C(\nu,d)),\\
 p(\omega)&=Ct_\omega,&
 g_\omega&=\epsilon_C(t_\omega R_{p(\omega)}^{-1}).
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{D.47.15}
\]
Let \(E_C\) be the group in \textup{(D.47.14)} with
\(C\backslash D\) and the outer pattern \(b_C\).
There is an actual injection over \(D\)
\[
 j_C:E_C\hookrightarrow E_* ,\qquad
 j_C(z,d)(\omega)=L(g_\omega)z(p(\omega))L(g_{\omega d})^{-1}.
 \tag{D.47.16}
\]
Its outer-coordinate identity is
\(\epsilon_*(k(\omega,d))=
g_\omega+b_C(d,p(\omega))-g_{\omega d}\).
The displayed factors in \(C\) prove this equality;
adjacent inverse factors prove the homomorphism identity.
Reading a coordinate above each \(\nu\) proves injectivity.
Also \(g_{\omega_0}=0\).

\paragraph{The actual source and every boundary root condition.}
Put \(K_j=\ker q_j\) and \(H_{j,C}=q_j^{-1}(C)\).
For words \(T_\omega\) with \(q_j(T_\omega)=t_\omega\)
and \(T_{\omega_0}=1\), twisted Shapiro is the explicit map
\[
 \begin{split}
 \varphi:H_{j,D_*}&\longrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}(S),
                      \qquad \epsilon\varphi=\epsilon_*q_j,\\
 z_\varphi(g)(\omega)
       &=\varphi(T_\omega gT_{\omega q_j(g)}^{-1}),\qquad
 f_\varphi(g)=(z_\varphi(g),q_j(g)).
 \end{split}
 \tag{D.47.17}
\]
Middle words cancel in every product. Conversely evaluate
the cocycle at \(\omega_0\) on \(H_{j,D_*}\).
The normalizing vector
\(v(\omega)=z(T_\omega)(\omega_0)\) belongs to \(S^\Omega\),
has \(v(\omega_0)=1\), and gives
\(z_\varphi(g)(\omega)=
v(\omega)z(g)(\omega)v(\omega q_j(g))^{-1}\).
These formulas are inverse normalizations, so each surface
map has exactly \(|S|^{|\Omega|-1}\) literal gauges.
They preserve the boundary \(A\)-classes and generation.
The analogous construction on \(C\backslash D\), followed
by \(j_C\), restricts at \(\omega_0\) to the very same
surface map on \(H_{j,D_*}\): here \(g_{\omega_0}=0\)
and \(D_*\) fixes that coordinate.

Conjugacy by \(A\) for two elements above the same base
element is equivalent to \(S\)-conjugacy of every
permutation-cycle product. Indeed the successive conjugator
equations determine each next coordinate from the preceding
one; their outer coordinates vanish, and the last equation
is precisely the cycle-product condition.
For a boundary \(\delta\) on \(C\backslash D\), choose
initial coordinate \(\nu\), and coordinates \(\omega\)
over it for all fine cycles \(\gamma\) of relative degree
\(m_\gamma\). The exact enlarged boundary subset
\(T_{j,C,\delta}\) is the intersection
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 a\in\widetilde S_{\operatorname{im}\epsilon_C},\qquad
 \epsilon(a)=\epsilon_C(q_j(c_\delta)),\\
 L(g_\omega)a^{m_\gamma}L(g_\omega)^{-1}
                     \in\mathcal C_{j,\gamma}
                         \quad\hbox{for every }\gamma.
 \end{gathered}
 \tag{D.47.18}
\]
The classes \(\mathcal C_{0,\gamma}\) come from the
actual cycle products of \(X_i\); those for \(j=1\)
come from \(H_iX_iH_i^{-1}\). These subsets retain all
roots and every empty intersection.

The actual boundary bijection between the two covers is
\[
 C d\langle q_1(x_i)\rangle
              \longmapsto C d h_i\langle d_i\rangle.
 \tag{D.47.19}
\]
It preserves lengths and every relative degree.
Take the old initial coordinate corresponding to a new
\(\nu'\) to be \(\nu'h_i\).
There is an actual element \(\mathcal L_i\in E_C\)
above \(h_i\), with components
\(\mathcal L_i(\nu)=L(b_C(h_i,\nu))\).
Its image under \(j_C\) and \(H_i\) differ by an element
of \(A\). Conjugating by \(\mathcal L_i\) therefore gives
the exact equality of complete boundary subsets
\[
 T_{1,C,\delta'}=
 L(b_C(h_i,\nu'))\,T_{0,C,\delta}\,L(b_C(h_i,\nu'))^{-1}.
 \tag{D.47.20}
\]
On a cycle product the conjugator is precisely this single
component of \(\mathcal L_i\). Its inverse proves the
reverse inclusion, including the intersections in
\textup{(D.47.18)}. The argument allows arbitrary given
\(X_i\); membership of \(X_i\) in \(j_C(E_C)\) is not
required for the conjugacy comparison.

Both source characters \(\epsilon_Cq_j|_{H_{j,C}}\)
have the same image \(\operatorname{im}\epsilon_C\),
since \(q_j(H_{j,C})=C\), and their matched boundary
values agree. Their standard surface presentations have
the same genus by \textup{(D.47.19)} and the degree formula.
Apply the exact character-matching maps above, then the
independent effective-phase maps to \textup{(D.47.20)}
and to the paths in the matching isomorphism.
Every such phase lies in \(\operatorname{im}\epsilon_C\).
This proves equality, for \(j=0,1\), of the numbers of
epimorphisms
\[
 H_{j,C}\twoheadrightarrow
         \widetilde S_{\operatorname{im}\epsilon_C}
 \tag{D.47.21}
\]
with their exact outer character and all conditions
\textup{(D.47.18)}.

\paragraph{Subtracting the identical finite-base maps.}
For an epimorphism in \textup{(D.47.21)}, its \(K_j\)-image
is normal in the target and contained in \(S\), hence is
either \(1\) or \(S\). The maps with image \(1\) are
exactly
\[
 \varphi=\Phi q_j|_{H_{j,C}},\qquad
 \Phi:C\twoheadrightarrow\widetilde S_{\operatorname{im}\epsilon_C},
                  \qquad\epsilon\Phi=\epsilon_C.
 \tag{D.47.22}
\]
Use the same actual \(\Phi\) on both sides. Its Shapiro
section over \(D\) is the homomorphism
\[
 s_\Phi:D\longrightarrow E_C,\qquad
 s_\Phi(d)(\nu)=\Phi(R_\nu dR_{\nu d}^{-1}),
               \quad\hbox{with base coordinate }d.
 \tag{D.47.23}
\]
It is independent of \(q_j\). Equations
\textup{(D.47.2)} and \textup{(D.47.23)} show that
\(j_Cs_\Phi(q_1(x_i))\) is the conjugate of
\(j_Cs_\Phi(d_i)\) by \(j_Cs_\Phi(h_i)\).
This conjugator and \(H_i\) have the same base value,
so their ratio belongs to \(A\). Thus the old boundary
condition holds for this \(\Phi\) exactly when the new
one does. This is a bijection of the precise subtracted
sets, and it retains all character-extension choices.
Subtracting their equal finite cardinalities from
\textup{(D.47.21)} gives equal counts of maps with
\(\varphi(K_j)=S\), for every actual intermediate
\(C\) and every extending \(\epsilon_C\).

\paragraph{Normalizer inversion and the entire generating fibre.}
For a surface map on \(H_{j,D_*}\) with \(K_j\)-image \(S\),
let \(N_\varphi=\ker(\varphi|_{K_j})\).
Its normalizer contains \(H_{j,D_*}\) and \(K_j\),
so it equals \(H_{j,C}\) for some \(C\geq D_*\).
The normalizer contains \(H_{j,C}\) precisely when
\(\varphi\) extends to \(H_{j,C}\to\operatorname{Aut}(S)\).
Conjugation on \(K_j/N_\varphi\simeq S\) constructs this
extension. It agrees with \(\varphi\) on \(H_{j,D_*}\)
and is unique: an automorphism centralizing all inner
automorphisms of the centerless group \(S\) fixes every
element of \(S\). Its outer coordinate factors through
one unique extending character \(\epsilon_C:C\to C_M\).
Its image is the full actual preimage
\(\widetilde S_{\operatorname{im}\epsilon_C}\), because
its \(K_j\)-image is \(S\). Conversely such an extension
normalizes \(N_\varphi\).

Let \(M_{j,C}\) be the sum, over every extending
\(\epsilon_C\), of the retained counts after
\textup{(D.47.22)}. The literal restriction comparison
for \(j_C\) proves that this counts exactly those
original surface maps whose kernel normalizer contains
\(H_{j,C}\). Uniqueness makes the summands disjoint.
The preceding paragraphs give \(M_{0,C}=M_{1,C}\).
Finite subgroup-poset inversion therefore gives
\[
 e_j=\sum_{D_*\leq C\leq D}\mu(D_*,C)M_{j,C},\qquad
 e_0=e_1,\qquad
 |\mathcal E(q_j;H_i)|=|S|^{|\Omega|-1}e_j,
 \tag{D.47.24}
\]
where on the old side the conjugators are \(1\).
To verify the last equality, minimal normalizer means
that the conjugate coordinate kernels on \(K_j\) are
pairwise distinct. The \(K_j\)-image is a subdirect
product of the simple factors. A proper such product
identifies two factors and their coordinate kernels:
apply the two-factor Goursat lemma inductively, using
that every normal subgroup of a product of nonabelian
simple groups is a product of factors. Thus minimal
normalizer gives exactly the full \(S^\Omega\)-image.
Together with the onto base map this is surjectivity
to \(E\). Conversely every onto map has precisely
these coordinate images and distinct kernels.
The gauge factor is the literal one from
\textup{(D.47.17)}. The given epimorphism \(q_E\)
has these properties, so \(e_0>0\). This proves the
complete fibre statement.

For completeness the ordinary conjugator union also has
an exact comparison. Let \(\mathcal C_i\) be the
\(A\)-class of \(X_i\), and let \(r_i\) be the size of
its orbit under \(C_D(d_i)\). This action is defined by
conjugating with any lift of the centralizer element;
two such lifts differ by \(A\), so the action on
\(A\)-classes is well-defined. Conjugation by \(H_i\)
identifies that orbit with the \(A\)-classes of all
\(E\)-conjugates of \(X_i\) above \(q_1(x_i)\).
Every class is obtained by replacing the specified base
conjugator \(h_i\) by \(h_ic_i\), with
\(c_i\in C_D(d_i)\). Different triples of these
\(A\)-classes give disjoint literal source fibres.
The established result applies to every one of these
triples and gives the same cardinality
\(|S|^{|\Omega|-1}e_0\). Consequently the complete
ordinary peripheral epimorphism fibre above either
base map has cardinality
\(r_1r_2r_3|S|^{|\Omega|-1}e_0\).
This proves the stated full-union assertion with all
base centralizer choices retained.

\paragraph{The specified pro-five and coupled sources.}
Use the actual D.37 source \(q_0=\rho_n\),
\(q_1=\beta_Q\rho_n\) and its displayed conjugators
\(1,f_Q,h_Q\). Equation \textup{(D.47.3)} supplies
the asserted generating lift above those exact maps.
Every homomorphism from \(S^\Omega\) to a finite
five-group is trivial: its image is both perfect and
a finite five-group, while every nontrivial finite
five-group has nontrivial abelianization. Hence
every such homomorphism from \(E\) factors uniquely
through \(P_n\), proving the stated maximal pro-five
quotient with its actual induced action.

More generally, let \(L\twoheadrightarrow D\) have
solvable kernel \(B\), and retain a given epimorphism
\(q_L:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow L\) above \(q_1\).
Combine the constructed \(f\) and \(q_L\) in
\(E\times_D L\). The \(K_1\)-image projects onto
both \(S^\Omega\) and \(B\). Its Goursat common
quotient is a solvable quotient of the perfect group
\(S^\Omega\), hence is trivial. Thus that image is
\(S^\Omega\times B\). The base image is \(D\),
so the combined source is onto the actual fibre
product and retains \(q_L\) literally.

\paragraph{Exact composite and nonsplit checks.}
The program \texttt{a\_cyclic\_outer\_composite.py}
retains all forty literal corrected push maps and
their inverses used in the twelve recorded moduli.
It verifies the complete nonunit-character and
boundary-supplier formulas, and all \(359268\)
genus-one handle/boundary characters in its orbit
checks. The proof above supplies the arbitrary
modulus and genus comparison.

The independent program
\texttt{a\_cyclic\_outer\_nonsplit.py}
uses the actual quotient \(Q_{16}\times C_3\to C_6\)
with kernel \(Q_8\). In coordinates its law and
projection are
\[
 \begin{split}
 (a,b,c)(x,y,z)&=
 (a+(-1)^b x+4by\bmod8,\ b+y\bmod2,\ c+z\bmod3),\\
 \epsilon(a,b,c)&=3(a\bmod2)+4c\pmod6.
 \end{split}
 \tag{D.47.25}
\]
The chosen lift \((1,0,1)\) has order \(24\);
every lift of \(1\in C_6\) has order \(12\) or \(24\),
so this quotient has no section. Over the actual
Heisenberg base \(\operatorname{Heis}(\mathbf Z/6)\),
the program checks all \(46656\) outer-cocycle
products, the six intermediate characters, the
actual gauge and embedding multiplications, \(804\)
nontrivial kernel carries, and \(6084\) literal
cycle-product transports. This verifies precisely
the nonsplit group identities used above; the
simple-kernel generation is proved by the displayed
normalizer and Goursat comparisons. Both programs,
their outputs, JSON data, and the nonsplit matrix
certificate are retained in \texttt{code/}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The full integral affine return tower}

\begin{statement}{D.48}{Proved}{An entire return-prime lattice tower with its literal inverse-limit fibre}
Retain the distinct primes \(\ell,p\geq5\), the integer
\(a=\operatorname{ord}_p(\ell)\), and the actual sources
\(\Gamma,D\) of D.46. Let \(\mathcal O\) be the
unramified extension of \(\mathbf Z_\ell\) of degree \(a\),
with the lift \(\widetilde\zeta\) of the specified
order-\(p\) element of its residue field. For
\(1\leq n<\infty\), put
\(\mathcal O_n=\mathcal O/\ell^n\mathcal O\), and
write \(\mathcal O_\infty=\mathcal O\).
Use the same cyclic shifts and diagonal actions to form
\[
 V_n=\mathcal O_n^\ell,\quad
 H_n=V_n\rtimes P,\quad
 q_{H_n}(x)=(e_0,c),\quad q_{H_n}(y)=(0,n_0).
 \tag{D.48.1}
\]
Let \(E_n\) be the actual closed six-coset image of
\(\widehat B\), using precisely D.46.5, and put
\[
 W_n=V_n^6,\qquad J_n=\Gamma\mathbin{\times_D}E_n.
 \tag{D.48.2}
\]
Then all these maps are epimorphisms, and
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \ker(E_n\to D)=\ker(J_n\to\Gamma)=W_n,\
 E_n=E_\infty/\ell^nW_\infty,\qquad
 J_n=J_\infty/\ell^nW_\infty,\qquad
 J_\infty\simeq\varprojlim_nJ_n.
 \end{gathered}
 \tag{D.48.3}
\]
The equalities retain the actual maps from \(\widehat B\).
In particular, for \(K=O^p(O^\ell(F))\), there is an
actual epimorphism
\[
 \widehat B/O^\ell(K)\twoheadrightarrow J_\infty
       \twoheadrightarrow\Gamma,
 \qquad\ker(J_\infty\to\Gamma)
          =\mathcal O^{6\ell}.
 \tag{D.48.4}
\]

Fix any one entire normalized old D.44 automorphism
\(\alpha\) of \(\Gamma\), including its literal
conjugator and prescribed old peripheral conjugators.
It has a normalized peripheral automorphism on this
whole \(J_\infty\) retaining all that data.
The maximal pro-\(\ell\) pure quotient is still the
original \(P_\ell\), with the specified original pair.
Thus the R8 weight-nine realization and the chosen
whole relative pro-\(p\) lift are retained through
this complete affine return tower.

Let \(\mathscr X_n\) be the full literal fibre of
normalized peripheral source maps to \(J_n\) above
this same old \(\alpha\), with \(\tau\) fixed.
Every map in the fibre is generating and factors
through an automorphism of this same \(J_n\).
After choosing one origin \(\sigma_0\) in the
infinite fibre, the actual maps give compatible
torsor isomorphisms
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 W_\infty^\tau\simeq\mathcal O^\ell
       &\longrightarrow\mathscr X_\infty,
       &w&\longmapsto\operatorname{Inn}(w)\sigma_0,\\
 W_n^\tau\simeq\mathcal O_n^\ell
       &\longrightarrow\mathscr X_n,
       &\bar w&\longmapsto
          \operatorname{Inn}(\bar w)(\sigma_0\bmod\ell^n),\\
 \mathscr X_\infty&\simeq\varprojlim_n\mathscr X_n,
       &&|\mathscr X_n|=\ell^{n\ell a}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{D.48.5}
\]
Every finite normalized map lifts to the entire
compatible tower. Before fixing \(\tau\), the full
peripheral fibre is a torsor under \(W_n\), with
\(\ell^{6n\ell a}\) literal maps at finite precision.
These are the full ordinary centralizer unions and
also the fibres with prescribed old conjugators;
no conjugator freedom is discarded.
The exact word-to-image fibres are specified in
\textup{(D.48.12)} below.
\end{statement}

\begin{proof}
We give integral source maps before using their finite reductions.
The derivative of \(T^p-1\) at the chosen residue
root is a unit, so its root has a unique lift in the
unramified degree-\(a\) extension. This gives
\(\widetilde\zeta^p=1\) literally, and
\(\widetilde\zeta^b-1\) is a unit whenever
\(b\not\equiv0\pmod p\).
The coefficient ring is
\(\mathcal O=\mathbf Z_\ell[\widetilde\zeta]\).
Thus every local multiplication in D.46 is defined
over this actual ring and reduces compatibly to
\(\mathcal O_n\).

The closed subgroup generated by the two elements
in \textup{(D.48.1)} maps onto \(P\).
The \(\ell\)-th power of the first is the
constant vector, whose conjugates span
\(\mathcal O^\ell\): apply the unit
\(\widetilde\zeta-1\) in one coordinate and
then use powers of \(\widetilde\zeta\) and
the cyclic shift. Integer powers and their
\(\mathbf Z_\ell\)-limits supply these coefficients
inside the closed source image. This proves
\(q_{H_\infty}\) is onto and supplies all its
finite quotient maps.

\paragraph{The actual whole kernel and all reductions.}
The source \(E_\infty\) is a closed subgroup of
\(H_\infty^6\rtimes\mathfrak S_3\), and its
kernel over \(D\) lies in \(\mathcal O^{6\ell}\).
Its reduction modulo \(\ell\) is the entire
kernel of D.46.3. One can see this with actual words:
the conjugates of the three cusp powers of exponent
\(\ell p\) retained in D.46 have a basis of the
modulo-\(\ell\) kernel among their vector images.
Lift those same words to \(E_\infty\).
The determinant of their vector matrix is a unit
in \(\mathbf Z_\ell\), so their
\(\mathbf Z_\ell\)-linear span is the whole
\(\mathcal O^{6\ell}\).
They commute inside this kernel, and continuous
powers realize all those coefficients in the
actual closed subgroup. Hence its kernel is
\(W_\infty=\mathcal O^{6\ell}\).
The same conclusion follows from the closed-module
form of Nakayama's lemma, applied to this specified
submodule of a finite free \(\mathbf Z_\ell\)-module.

Reduction of all six components now has kernel
exactly \(\ell^n W_\infty\), which proves
the asserted \(E_n\) maps in
\textup{(D.48.3)}. Every finite image and
every transition is therefore the image of the
same two source generators.
The commutator map satisfies
\[
 [E_{\infty,F},W_\infty]=W_\infty,
 \qquad W_n^D=0\quad(1\leq n\leq\infty).
 \tag{D.48.6}
\]
For the first equality its reduction modulo
\(\ell\) is onto by D.46.8. The sum of the
images of the two integral operators for
\(x-1,y-1\) is a closed submodule and has
a unit full-rank minor, hence is all of
\(W_\infty\). For the second, a fixed vector
at finite precision reduces to zero modulo
\(\ell\) by D.46.8; divide by \(\ell\)
and induct on the precision. The infinite
assertion follows from all these reductions.

\paragraph{Integral centralizer equations and the entire union.}
The local equations used in D.46 remain exact over
every \(\mathcal O_n\). For the cyclic shift
\(C\) on \(\mathcal O_n^\ell\),
\[
 \ker(1-C)=\mathcal O_n\sum_i e_i,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{im}(1-C)
      =\{(v_i):\textstyle\sum_i v_i=0\}.
 \tag{D.48.7}
\]
Both equalities follow by successively solving
the coordinate differences, and use no division
by \(\ell\). The \(Y\) fixed space consists
of the vectors with first coordinate zero,
because \(\widetilde\zeta-1\) is a unit.
The operator \(1-Z\) is invertible: since
\(Z=(XY)^{-1}\), its linear action satisfies
\(Z^\ell=\widetilde\zeta^{-1}I\), and its inverse is
\((1+Z+\cdots+Z^{\ell-1})/(1-\widetilde\zeta^{-1})\).
The displayed denominator is a unit.

Summing the \(X\) centralizer equation still
forces the constant \(N\)-coordinate to vanish,
so the first local image in D.46.10 is again
exactly \(\langle c\rangle\).
The \(Y\) and \(Z\) centralizer projections
are still onto. The unchanged actual
\(F^{\rm ab}/p\) quotient and the two-cycle
coordinate equations of D.46 then give
\[
 C_{E_n}(s)\twoheadrightarrow C_D(s),\quad
 C_{E_n}(r)\twoheadrightarrow C_D(r),\quad
 C_{E_n}(\tau)\twoheadrightarrow C_D(\tau)
       \quad(1\leq n\leq\infty).
 \tag{D.48.8}
\]
All corrections are in the actual full kernel
\(W_n\).

The invariant modules at \(s,r,\tau\) are free
over \(\mathcal O_n\) of ranks
\(3\ell,2\ell,\ell\), respectively.
For \(\tau\), choose one coordinate in each
of its three two-cycles. The three choices
are a constant vector for \(X\), a vector
with first coordinate zero for \(Y\), and
zero for \(Z\). The partner coordinates
are prescribed by the actual \(\tau\)
action. This is an explicit compatible
isomorphism
\(W_n^\tau\simeq\mathcal O_n\oplus
\mathcal O_n^{\ell-1}\).
In particular every invariant vector at
finite precision lifts invariantly to
\(W_\infty\).

\paragraph{Existence, full fibres, and generation over the ring.}
Choose lifts in \(E_\infty\) of the prescribed
three conjugators in \(D\). Their product
defect lies in \(W_\infty\).
The exact correction map D.23.8 is now a
\(\mathbf Z_\ell\)-linear map
\(W_\infty^3\to W_\infty\).
Its reduction modulo \(\ell\) is onto by
D.46.12; a unit minor therefore gives an
actual integral right inverse.
Cancelling the defect produces a continuous
peripheral source map \(\widehat B\to E_\infty\).
It factors through \(\widehat B\) from the
three-boundary source because its first two
images are conjugate to the actual elements
of orders two and three.

Every such source map is onto, at every
precision. Its image projects onto \(D\)
and contains the \(2\ell p\)-th power of
the prescribed \(\tau\) conjugate.
This is a vector whose reduction in
\(W_1\) is nonzero. Its orbit spans
the irreducible \(D\)-module \(W_1\).
The image's intersection with \(W_n\)
is a closed \(D\)-invariant
\(\mathbf Z_\ell\)-submodule; it therefore
surjects onto \(W_1\), and Nakayama gives
that it is the whole \(W_n\).
This proves generation, including at
\(n=\infty\).

At finite precision the correction solutions
in conjugators number \(|W_n|^2\).
Using the three free invariant modules just
computed gives exactly
\(\ell^{6n\ell a}=|W_n|\) distinct maps.
The surjections \textup{(D.48.8)} identify
this with the full ordinary conjugator union.
By \textup{(D.48.6)} the kernel-conjugation
action is free, so the maps form exactly
one \(W_n\)-orbit.
The infinite fibre is also one free
\(W_\infty\)-orbit: after choosing one
solution, its comparison with any other
has a unique conjugator at each finite
precision. Uniqueness makes these conjugators
compatible, and their inverse limit gives
the required element of \(W_\infty\).
Fixing \(\tau\) is precisely restriction
to the invariant subgroup \(W_n^\tau\).

\paragraph{Actual automorphisms and the whole retained old quotient.}
The pure rigidity proof of D.46 works over
\(\mathcal O_n\) without a new equation.
The first translation has coordinate sum
\(\widetilde\zeta^b\); equation
\textup{(D.48.7)} arranges it in the first
coordinate, a constant \(N\)-element
removes its scalar, and the remaining
\(V_n^c\) action removes the second
translation using the unit
\(1-\widetilde\zeta\).
Every pure peripheral source map to
\(H_n\) over the identity on \(P\)
is consequently an inner conjugate of
the specified source map.

For a normalized source map to \(E_n\),
\textup{(D.48.6)} places its normalized
conjugator in \(E_{n,F}'\). Its identity
coordinate is therefore a pure map of
the preceding kind. The six actual
conjugates in D.46.13 prove preservation
of the same closed normal core, also
when \(n=\infty\). Thus the source map
factors through an onto endomorphism of
this same \(E_n\). These groups are
finitely generated profinite quotients
of \(\widehat B\), and hence Hopfian;
the endomorphism is an automorphism.
Kernel conjugation handles the full
unnormalized fibre as well.

The image of the old source kernel \(K\)
in \(E_\infty\) is the entire
\(W_\infty\). It is contained there
because \(D\) is an old quotient.
Its reduction is all of \(W_1\) by
D.46.14. It is a closed
\(\mathbf Z_\ell\)-submodule, so the
same unit-basis argument gives
\[
 q_{E_\infty}(K)=W_\infty.
 \tag{D.48.9}
\]
Consequently the actual joint source
is the complete fibre product in
\textup{(D.48.2)}. Componentwise
automorphisms on \(\Gamma\) and
\(E_n\), agreeing on \(D\), give
its actual automorphisms, and every
peripheral source map above the fixed
old automorphism has this factorization.
Pairing the old conjugators with upper
conjugators having their exact
\(D\)-images retains those whole old
conjugators. Since \([J_{n,F},W_n]=W_n\),
the new normalized conjugator belongs
to \(J_{n,F}'\) and has precisely the
given old image.

The source kernel of \(J_\infty\)
contains \(O^\ell(K)\), since its
image on \(K\) is the pro-\(\ell\)
group in \textup{(D.48.9)}.
This proves \textup{(D.48.4)}.
The source kernel also lies in
\(O^\ell(F)\). Every finite
\(\ell\)-quotient of the new pure
group, composed with its source map
from \(F\), factors through the
original \(P_\ell\), which is itself
a quotient of the new pure group.
This proves the exact maximal
pro-\(\ell\) comparison and retains
the original action on it.

\paragraph{The full inverse-limit and word fibres.}
The quotient maps in
\textup{(D.48.3)} identify each
\(\ell^nW_\infty\) as the literal
source descent kernel. An automorphism
above the specified old map preserves
\(W_\infty\), and therefore preserves
each of these characteristic subgroups
of its kernel. All the displayed
transition maps on full fibres are
thus actual descent maps.
With one infinite origin selected,
their parameters are exactly the
reductions of \(W_\infty^\tau\).
Every such finite parameter lifts,
and a compatible collection has
one inverse-limit parameter.
This proves all comparisons in
\textup{(D.48.5)}, including their
topology: the continuous bijection
from the compact parameter group
to the closed source-map fibre is
a homeomorphism.

Writing \(f_0=s\sigma_0(s)\) for
the new infinite origin, the
conjugator image at parameter
\(w\in W_\infty^\tau\) is the
literal group expression
\[
       f(w)=(sws)f_0w^{-1}\in J_{\infty,F}'.
 \tag{D.48.10}
\]
Its old image is the specified
old \(f\), because \(w\) lies
in the kernel over \(\Gamma\).
The parameterization is injective:
equality of these conjugators
would give the same normalized
map on both \(s\) and \(\tau\),
hence on \(s,r\); its kernel
stabilizer is zero by
\textup{(D.48.6)}.
At finite precision the same
formula uses \(\bar w\), and
\[
     \mathscr X_{n+1}\longrightarrow\mathscr X_n
        \quad\hbox{is the surjective reduction}
        \quad\mathcal O_{n+1}^\ell\to\mathcal O_n^\ell.
 \tag{D.48.11}
\]
Finally each image in
\textup{(D.48.10)} has, after
choosing one source preimage
\(\widetilde f(w)\in F'\),
the complete profinite word fibre
\[
 \widetilde f(w)\,
    \ker\bigl(F'\longrightarrow J_{\infty,F}'\bigr).
 \tag{D.48.12}
\]
The analogous expression applies
at every finite precision.
This separates the full word
fibres from the affine lattice
of conjugator images.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The uniform signed quotient and the full congruence correction}

\begin{statement}{E.53}{Proved}{The integral common source with the complete double cover}
Retain E.52's actual maps $\rho_m,\rho_R,\Phi_m,\Phi_R$,
where $R=\prod_{p\geq5}\mathbf Z_p$, and retain
$\rho_L:\widehat B\twoheadrightarrow G_L$ from E.38--E.43.
Write $Q_T=\Phi_T(1,V_3(T))\subset C_T$ for
$T=\mathbf Z/m$ or $R$.
For $m>1$ prime to six, the actual modular map
\[
 q_{4m}:\widehat B\twoheadrightarrow
       Q_{4m}=\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf Z/4m)/\{\pm I\},
 \quad
 s\longmapsto\left[\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}\right],
 \quad
 r\longmapsto\left[\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}\right]
 \tag{E.53.1}
\]
factors through $\rho_m$. Together with the ordinary
exponent quotient of E.52 it gives the actual isomorphism
\[
 G_m/Q_m\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal J_m,
 \qquad
 \mathcal J_m=A_{2m}\mathbin{\times_{A_2}}Q_{4m},
 \qquad |\mathcal J_m|=24m^2|\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf Z/m)|.
 \tag{E.53.2}
\]
The two maps to $A_2$ are reduction of exponent sums
modulo two and projective matrix reduction modulo four.
Their values on $s,r$ are the same displayed source values.
Every comparison in \textup{(E.53.2)} commutes with
reduction of $m$.

Put $\mathcal J_1=A_2$, and retain the E.50 epimorphism
$G_L\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal J_5$.
The maximum common quotient for the specified maps
$(\rho_L,\rho_R)$ is exactly $\mathcal J_5$.
For finite $m$ it is $\mathcal J_{\gcd(m,5)}$.
Equivalently their actual joint images are
\[
 \begin{split}
 \operatorname{im}(\rho_L,\rho_R)
       &=G_L\mathbin{\times_{\mathcal J_5}}G_R,\\
 \operatorname{im}(\rho_L,\rho_m)
       &=G_L\mathbin{\times_{\mathcal J_{\gcd(m,5)}}}G_m.
 \end{split}
 \tag{E.53.3}
\]
These are equalities of the source images under the
displayed projections.

Let $\Gamma_5(1)=\ker(\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf Z_5)
\to\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf F_5))$.
The exact correcting-subgroup image is
\[
 \begin{split}
 \rho_R(R_{\mathrm{nil}}\cap\ker\rho_L)
   =\Phi_R\left(
       \Gamma_5(1)\times\prod_{p\geq7}\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf Z_p),
                           V_3(R)\right)
   =:\mathcal K_R.
 \end{split}
 \tag{E.53.4}
\]
Intersecting the source on the left with
$\ker\rho_{D_{23}}$ leaves that image unchanged.
Intersecting additionally with $\ker\rho_5\cap\ker\rho_7$
gives precisely
\[
 \begin{split}
 \mathcal K_R^{35}
   =\Phi_R\left(
       \Gamma_5(1)\times\Gamma_7(1)
          \times\prod_{p\geq11}\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf Z_p),
          \ 5V_3(\mathbf Z_5)\times7V_3(\mathbf Z_7)
               \times\prod_{p\geq11}V_3(\mathbf Z_p)\right).
 \end{split}
 \tag{E.53.5}
\]
Here the argument of $\Phi_R$ is the displayed element
of $\operatorname{SL}_2(R)\times V_3(R)$.
Each prescribed target value in either correcting image
has the full source fibre $k\ker(\rho_R|_K)$, where
$K$ is the corresponding displayed intersection and
$k\in K$ is one preimage.
Every such correction maps to the identity in every
nilpotent continuous quotient of $\widehat H$.
\end{statement}

\begin{proof}
We retain the central sign first, and then determine
the kernel of each actual joint source map.

\paragraph{The canonical signed matrix on the pure subgroup.}
For a pure word $f\in F$, its ordinary integral modular
matrix is determined up to its central sign. Exactly
one sign has both diagonal entries equal to one modulo
four. Indeed the off-diagonal entries are even, and
determinant one makes the two odd diagonal residues
equal modulo four. Products of matrices with diagonal
entries one modulo four retain that property.
The sign choice therefore defines a homomorphism on
the pure subgroup, with
\[
 x\longmapsto\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 y\longmapsto\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-2&1\end{pmatrix}.
 \tag{E.53.6}
\]
For finite quotients this means the compatible CRT
representative with the indicated component modulo four;
it also defines the corresponding continuous pure map.
With $P=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$,
its component modulo $m$ is $P\theta(f)P$.
For exponent sums $(a,b)$ its component modulo four is
\[
                   \begin{pmatrix}1&2a\\-2b&1\end{pmatrix}.
 \tag{E.53.7}
\]
Both assertions follow on the two free generators
from \textup{(E.53.6)} and extend by multiplication.
In particular $Q_4\simeq A_2$ through this exact map.

An element of $\ker\rho_m$ lies in $K_2$ by E.52's
two parity characters and has $\theta$-value one.
Equations \textup{(E.53.6)--(E.53.7)} make its
canonical matrix the identity modulo $4m$.
Thus $q_{4m}$ factors through $G_m$.
It is onto: the product of the displayed $s,r$ matrices
is $E_{12}(-1)$; its powers and conjugation by $s$
give all upper and lower elementary matrices.
Elementary elimination over each prime-power factor
and CRT prove generation of the full determinant-one
group, hence of its specified projective quotient.

The kernel of $G_m\to A_{2m}$ is $C_m$.
On $C_m$, the modular map has trivial four-component
and its signed $m$-component is exactly $P\theta P$.
The common kernel is consequently $Q_m$.
The image of $G_m/Q_m$ lies in the actual fibre
product in \textup{(E.53.2)}.
Now $|Q_{4m}|=24|\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf Z/m)|$,
because $|\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf Z/4)|=48$ and
the diagonal central sign has order two.
The fibre product therefore has the order stated in
\textup{(E.53.2)}, equal to $|G_m/Q_m|$ by E.52.
The injective map is onto. This proves both the
signed comparison and every transition map.

\paragraph{Finite quotients of the integral $\operatorname{SL}_2$ factor.}
We give the group facts needed to control the full
inverse system, including its central quotients.
For $p\geq5$ put
$L_p=\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf Z_p)$ and
$\Gamma_p(n)=\ker(L_p\to\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf Z/p^n))$.
The map
\[
 \Gamma_p(n)/\Gamma_p(n+1)\longrightarrow\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbf F_p),
              \qquad 1+p^n A\longmapsto A\bmod p
 \tag{E.53.8}
\]
is an isomorphism of additive groups and is equivariant
for the actual conjugation action of $L_p$.
The determinant equation gives trace zero; the two
elementary matrices and $\operatorname{diag}(1+p^na,(1+p^na)^{-1})$
give every basis vector, proving surjectivity.

This adjoint module is irreducible.
Conjugation by $E_{12}(t)$ and $E_{21}(t)$ is a
polynomial of degree at most two in $t$.
Interpolation at $0,1,-1$ shows that an invariant
subspace is stable under brackets with the usual
$e,f$, and hence with $h=[e,f]$.
The $h$-weights $0,2,-2$ are distinct for $p\geq5$.
Projection onto those three eigenspaces, followed
by brackets with $e,f$, shows that any nonzero
invariant subspace contains $e,f,h$.

Let $U\triangleleft L_p$ be open.
The group $\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbf F_p)$ is simple
by the following concrete argument. Its faithful
projective action is primitive; the translations form
an abelian normal subgroup of a point stabilizer,
and their conjugates generate the group. The elementary
commutators E.52.17 make it perfect.
A nontrivial normal subgroup is transitive in this
primitive faithful action. Modulo that subgroup,
all conjugate translation groups have the same
abelian image, because every group element is a
product of a normal-subgroup element and a point
stabilizer. The quotient is abelian, and perfectness
makes it trivial. This proves simplicity.
Consequently the reduction of $U$ modulo $p$ is
central or is the whole group. In the latter case
$L_p/U$ is a finite $p$-group. It is also perfect
by E.52.17, so it is trivial.

In the former case consider $U\cap\Gamma_p(1)$.
Let $n$ be the first layer in \textup{(E.53.8)}
where it has nonzero image. Irreducibility makes
that image the whole layer. Choose three elements
of $U$ giving a basis there.
For $a\geq1$, direct binomial expansion gives
\[
           (1+p^a A)^p\equiv1+p^{a+1}A\pmod{p^{a+2}}.
 \tag{E.53.9}
\]
Successive powers of the chosen elements therefore
span every later layer. Successive approximation
and closedness prove
$U\cap\Gamma_p(1)=\Gamma_p(n)$.
The reduction of $U$ is either $1$ or $\{\pm I\}$.
In the second case write an element above $-I$ as
$-v$ with $v\in\Gamma_p(1)$.
Its square lies in $\Gamma_p(n)$.
The finite $p$-group $\Gamma_p(1)/\Gamma_p(n)$
has no element of order two, so $v\in\Gamma_p(n)$.
Thus the possibilities are precisely
\[
                  U=\Gamma_p(n),\quad
                  U=\{\pm I\}\Gamma_p(n),\quad U=L_p.
 \tag{E.53.10}
\]
The argument also proves that any closed normal
subgroup with a nonzero first congruence layer
contains all of $\Gamma_p(1)$.

Every nontrivial finite quotient of $L_p$ therefore
has $\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbf F_p)$ as a
composition factor, and its centre has exponent
dividing two. For the last assertion a matrix
commuting with the two elementary generators is
scalar, and the determinant equation gives $\pm I$.
For a quotient by the central sign, reduce first
modulo $p$. A central projective element is scalar
there; its commutators with the elementary generators
are consequently both signs with reduction $+1$,
so they equal $+1$ before taking the quotient.
The same scalar calculation finishes that case.

A continuous finite quotient of $\prod_{p\geq5}L_p$
uses finitely many factors. Their images commute
and generate it. If a product of elements from
these factor images is central, each factor element
commutes with its own factor image, because all
other factor images commute with that image already.
Each factor element has square one by the preceding
paragraph, so the whole central product has square
one. We have proved that every such finite quotient
has centre of exponent dividing two.

\paragraph{The exact lower-central correcting image.}

                       M=\ker(G_R\to\mathcal J_5).
 \tag{E.53.12}

\subsection{An exact return-prime cover retaining the entire old pair}

\begin{statement}{D.46}{Proved}{A strict mixed return cover with its complete generating peripheral fibre}
Let \(\ell,p\geq5\) be distinct primes, put
\(a=\operatorname{ord}_p(\ell)\), and choose
\(k=\mathbf F_{\ell^a}\) with an element \(\zeta\) of order \(p\).
Indices below lie in \(\mathbf Z/\ell\).
Let \(c\) cyclically permute coordinates, put
\[
 N=(\mathbf F_p)^\ell,\quad
 P=N\rtimes\langle c\rangle,\quad
 V=k^\ell,\quad H=V\rtimes P,
 \qquad
 n(v_i)_i=(\zeta^{n_i}v_i)_i.
 \tag{D.46.1}
\]
These are specified actions, and the action of \(c\) on both
\(N\) and \(V\) is the same cyclic shift.
Retain the actual source \(\widehat B,F,s,r,\tau,x,y,z\) of D.44.
There is an epimorphism
\[
 q_H:F\twoheadrightarrow H,
 \qquad x\longmapsto X=(e_0,c),\quad
 y\longmapsto Y=(0,n_0),\quad z\longmapsto Z=(XY)^{-1},
 \tag{D.46.2}
\]
where \(n_0\) is the first coordinate vector of \(N\), and
\(e_0\) is the first coordinate vector of \(V\).
Let \(E\to D\) be the actual six-coset induced images of
\(\widehat B\) obtained from \(q_H\) and its projection
\(q_P:F\to P\), respectively, as specified in
\textup{(D.46.5)} below. Then
\[
 1\longrightarrow W=V^6\longrightarrow E\longrightarrow D
 \longrightarrow1,
 \qquad \dim_{\mathbf F_\ell}W=d=6\ell a.
 \tag{D.46.3}
\]
The \(D\)-module \(W\) is irreducible and nontrivial.

Put \(K=O^p(O^\ell(F))\) and
\(\Gamma=\widehat B/K\).
Every D.44 normalized automorphism of this entire \(\Gamma\)
induces an automorphism of the specified \(D\), and has a lift
to the actual joint source
\[
 J=\Gamma\mathbin{\times_D}E
   =\widehat B/(K\cap\ker q_E).
 \tag{D.46.4}
\]
The lift fixes \(\tau\), retains the complete old normalized
conjugator in \(\Gamma\), and has its new conjugator in the
image of \(F'\). Thus it retains the entire R8 pro-\(\ell\)
pair and the chosen whole relative pro-\(p\) lift of D.44.
The maximal pro-\(\ell\) quotient of the pure subgroup of
\(J\) is exactly \(P_\ell\), with the original action.

For the specified old automorphism, the complete literal
peripheral fibre before fixing \(\tau\) has \(\ell^d\)
elements. Every one generates the actual joint source and
factors through an automorphism of that source.
This fibre is one free \(W\)-conjugacy orbit.
The same set is obtained with any prescribed three base
conjugators, including the projections of prescribed old
conjugators in \(\Gamma\).
Fixing \(\tau\) gives precisely
\(\ell^{\ell a}\) literal normalized maps, a free transitive
orbit of \(W^\tau\). These counts concern maps and their
conjugator images; the complete profinite word fibres are
the cosets described in \textup{(D.46.17)}.

The source in \textup{(D.46.4)} is an actual quotient of
the return cover
\(\widehat B/O^\ell(O^p(O^\ell(F)))\), with a
nontrivial finite kernel over \(\Gamma\).
In contrast, adjacent repetition of one residual has the
exact identity \(O^p(O^p L)=O^p L\) for every profinite
group \(L\).
\end{statement}

\begin{proof}
We give the source construction and all descent maps explicitly.
Choose the six representatives \(t_i\) of \(B/F\) used in
D.44, with \(t_0=1\). For \(b\in\widehat B\), let
\(j=i\cdot\bar b\) in the regular right action of
\(\mathfrak S_3\), and put
\[
 q_E(b)=\left((i\mapsto j),
           \bigl(q_H(t_i b t_j^{-1})\bigr)_i\right),
 \qquad
 q_D(b)=\left((i\mapsto j),
           \bigl(q_P(t_i b t_j^{-1})\bigr)_i\right).
 \tag{D.46.5}
\]
The formula is first evaluated on the two literal generators
\(s,r\), and gives their continuous maps from the profinite
free product. In fact
\(t_i b b' t_k^{-1}=(t_i b t_j^{-1})(t_j b't_k^{-1})\);
this proves the multiplication rule, the two source relations,
and the displayed projections. The kernels are the corresponding
normal cores of \(\ker q_H\) and \(\ker q_P\) in
\(\widehat B\). Both images retain the specified
\(\mathfrak S_3\) quotient. No additional quotient kernel
is being presumed invariant under a changed source map.

\paragraph{The two-generator group and its residuals.}
The images of \(X,Y\) generate \(P\): conjugating \(n_0\)
by powers of \(c\) gives every coordinate generator of \(N\).
Moreover \(X^\ell=\sum_i e_i\ne0\) in \(V\).
Acting on this vector by \(n_0-1\) gives
\((\zeta-1)e_0\); powers of \(n_0\), their
\(\mathbf F_\ell\)-linear combinations, and the cyclic
shift generate all of \(V\), because
\(\mathbf F_\ell[\zeta]=k\).
This proves the epimorphism \textup{(D.46.2)}.
The same calculation proves that \(V\) is simple as an
\(\mathbf F_\ell[P]\)-module. Indeed the distinct
coordinate characters of the prime-to-\(\ell\) subgroup
\(N\) give its \(\ell\) simple coordinate summands
over \(\mathbf F_\ell\); \(c\) permutes them transitively.

The following are equalities with their quotient maps:
\[
 O^\ell(H)=V\rtimes N,
 \qquad O^p(V\rtimes N)=V,
 \qquad O^\ell(V)=1,
 \qquad O^\ell(P)=N,\quad O^p(N)=1.
 \tag{D.46.6}
\]
For the first equality, every finite \(\ell\)-quotient kills
\(N\), and therefore kills \([V,N]=V\); the remaining
quotient is the displayed \(C_\ell\). For the second,
every finite \(p\)-quotient kills \(V\), and the quotient
by \(V\) is the displayed \(p\)-group \(N\).
The last two identities follow by the same source projections.

The action of \(X\) on \(V\) is the cyclic permutation,
the action of \(Y\) changes only the first coordinate by
\(\zeta\), and the action of \(XY\) has its \(\ell\)-th
power equal to \(\zeta I\). Consequently
\[
 \begin{array}{c|ccc}
       &X&Y&Z\\ \hline
 \text{order in }H&\ell^2&p&\ell p\\
 \text{order in }P&\ell&p&\ell p\\
 \dim_{\mathbf F_\ell}V^{(\cdot)}&a&(\ell-1)a&0.
 \end{array}
 \tag{D.46.7}
\]
For \(XY\), the operator \(XY-1\) is invertible since
\((XY)^\ell=\zeta I\); hence the translation part of
\((XY)^{\ell p}\) vanishes, giving its asserted order.

\paragraph{The entire induced kernel.}
The kernel of \(E\to D\) is a submodule of \(V^6\).
The restrictions of its six ambient summands to the image of
\(F\) are simple. Their fixed-space profiles on the same
\(x,y,z\) are the six permutations of
\((a,(\ell-1)a,0)\), by the actual peripheral
\(\mathfrak S_3\) permutations in D.44.
They are therefore pairwise nonisomorphic.
For every summand one of
\(x^{\ell p},y^{\ell p},z^{\ell p}\) has nonzero
projection in that summand and is killed in \(D\):
use the \(X\) coordinate in \textup{(D.46.7)}.
Its normal closure surjects onto that simple summand.
A submodule of a direct sum of pairwise nonisomorphic simple
modules which surjects onto each summand is the whole direct
sum. This follows, for example, by splitting a submodule of
the semisimple module and using the absence of homomorphisms
between distinct simple summands; it does not require the
whole ambient group algebra to be semisimple.
Thus the kernel is precisely \(W=V^6\).
The \(\mathfrak S_3\) quotient permutes these six simple
summands transitively, so \(W\) is simple for \(D\).
In particular
\[
 W^D=0,
 \qquad W_D=0,
 \qquad [E_F,W]=W\subset E_F',
 \quad E_F=\operatorname{im}(F\to E).
 \tag{D.46.8}
\]

The action of \(s\) on the six summands has three two-cycles,
and the action of \(r\) has two three-cycles. Their powers
are literally the identity, so their invariant dimensions
are \(d/2,d/3\). The action of \(\tau\) has three
two-cycles and \(\tau^2=x^{-1}\). On a two-cycle its
fixed vectors are exactly the fixed vectors of \(x\) on
one chosen summand. Formula \textup{(D.46.7)} gives
\[
 \dim W^s=3\ell a,\qquad
 \dim W^r=2\ell a,\qquad
 \dim W^\tau=\ell a.
 \tag{D.46.9}
\]
Also the orders of \(\tau\) in \(D,E\) are respectively
\(2\ell p,2\ell^2p\), by \(\tau^2=x^{-1}\) and
\textup{(D.46.7)}.

\paragraph{All centralizer projections and all conjugator choices.}
For \(s,r\), the maps from the upper centralizers to the
lower centralizers are onto. A lift of a lower centralizer
element conjugates the chosen upper element to another
lift of the same cyclic subgroup; averaging over its order
\(2\) or \(3\), which is invertible in
\(\mathbf F_\ell\), supplies the required kernel
conjugator. Equivalently, this is the explicit coprime
cyclic-complement argument of D.44.

For \(\tau\) we verify the extra assertion directly.
The local centralizer projections are
\[
 \begin{split}
 C_H(X)&\longrightarrow\langle c\rangle
                    \subset C_P(c)=\langle c\rangle\times Z(P),\\
 C_H(Y)&\twoheadrightarrow C_P(n_0)=N,\\
 C_H(Z)&\twoheadrightarrow C_P(q_P(z)).
 \end{split}
 \tag{D.46.10}
\]
The image in the first line is exactly \(\langle c\rangle\).
Indeed an element of \(C_P(c)\) has its \(N\)-coordinate
constant, say \(b\); summing the coordinates of the
translation equation for commuting with \(X\) gives
\(1=\zeta^b\), hence \(b=0\). Powers of \(X\)
give every power of \(c\). The second line has the
literal commuting lifts \((0,n)\). For the third,
\(1-Z\) is invertible on \(V\); the translation
equation therefore has one solution for each lower
centralizer element.

The pure image in \(D\) retains the actual quotient
\(F^{\rm ab}/p\simeq\mathbf F_p^2\).
The second abelian coordinate is the sum of the
\(N\)-coordinates in the identity component of
\textup{(D.46.5)}, and conjugating by \(s\) recovers
the first. Conjugation by \(\tau\) sends these coordinates
\((u,v)\) to \((u-v,-v)\), since it fixes \(x\)
and interchanges the other two peripheral classes.
An element of the pure image centralizing \(\tau\)
therefore has \(v=0\). In the identity component its
projection to \(C_P(c)\) has constant \(N\)-coordinate
\(b\) with \(\ell b=0\) in \(\mathbf F_p\), so
\(b=0\). Its projection belongs to the image in the
first line of \textup{(D.46.10)}.

For clarity, the passage from these local tests to the
induced centralizer follows from the multiplication in
\textup{(D.46.5)}. On a two-cycle of \(\tau\), choose
one coordinate of a lift of a commuting element. Its
partner coordinate is forced by the commutation equation;
consistency of the second equation is precisely commutation
of the chosen coordinate with \(\tau^2\).
The three tests in \textup{(D.46.10)} supply those coordinates.
Their independent corrections are available because the
kernel is the entire \(V^6\). A general element of
\(C_D(\tau)\) has \(\mathfrak S_3\)-projection either
\(1\) or \(\bar\tau\); multiplication by \(\tau^{-1}\)
reduces the latter to the pure case just checked.
We have proved the three actual epimorphisms
\[
 C_E(s)\twoheadrightarrow C_D(s),\quad
 C_E(r)\twoheadrightarrow C_D(r),\quad
 C_E(\tau)\twoheadrightarrow C_D(\tau).
 \tag{D.46.11}
\]
Their kernels are respectively the three spaces in
\textup{(D.46.9)}.

\paragraph{The complete generating fibre.}
Apply the explicit product equation D.23.8 to
\((s,r,\tau^{-1})\). Since \(W_D=0\), its correction
map from \(W^3\) onto \(W\) is surjective for every
prescribed triple of lower conjugators.
Its solution set in conjugators has size \(|W|^2\).
Dividing only by the three kernel centralizers gives
\[
 \frac{|W|^2}{|W^s||W^r||W^\tau|}=|W|.
 \tag{D.46.12}
\]
The epimorphisms \textup{(D.46.11)} show that allowing
all lower centralizer choices gives the same set, rather
than enlarging it: every such change has a lift already
centralizing the corresponding upper peripheral element.
Thus \textup{(D.46.12)} is also the full ordinary
conjugator-union count.

Every solution generates \(E\). Its image surjects onto
\(D\), and its intersection with the irreducible \(W\)
is either \(W\) or zero. In the latter case the image
would be a complement isomorphic to \(D\). It cannot
contain the prescribed conjugate of \(\tau\), whose
upper order \(2\ell^2p\) exceeds its lower order
\(2\ell p\). This excludes the complement case.
The stabilizer of such a generating map under kernel
conjugation is \(W^D=0\). The count in
\textup{(D.46.12)} is therefore exactly one free orbit.
Fixing \(\tau\) cuts that orbit out by \(W^\tau\),
and yields exactly \(\ell^{\ell a}\) maps.

\paragraph{The pure rigidity that proves actual kernel preservation.}
We need an actual quotient automorphism, so we next prove
the source-kernel comparison.
Consider all peripheral epimorphisms \(F\to H\) above
the identity source map \(q_P\). A conjugate of \(X\)
over \(c\) has translation vector whose coordinate sum
is one of the \(p\) values \(\zeta^b\); every vector
with such a sum occurs. A conjugate of \(Y\) over
\(n_0\) has arbitrary translation in \(k e_0\).
Every lift of \(q_P(z)\) is a conjugate of \(Z\),
because \(1-Z\) is invertible. Thus their total number
is \(p|k|^\ell\), and every one generates: its
\(\ell\)-th power at the first cusp gives a nonzero
constant vector, whose \(P\)-orbit spans \(V\).

These maps are exactly one conjugacy orbit under
\(\pi^{-1}Z(P)\). Conjugation by \(V\) first arranges
the first translation to be \(\zeta^b e_0\); the
constant \(N\)-element removes \(\zeta^b\).
The remaining \(V^c=k\sum_i e_i\) conjugation changes
the second translation by \((1-\zeta)k e_0\), and
therefore sets it to zero. The centre of \(H\) is
trivial, so this also accounts for the entire orbit.
After \(X\) is fixed literally, the orbit is exactly
the free \(V^c\)-orbit. In particular every such source
map has precisely the kernel of \(q_H\).

Let now \(\phi:\widehat B\to E\) be any normalized
solution in the preceding fibre, so \(\phi(\tau)=\tau\).
Its conjugator \(f=s\phi(s)\) projects to the given
element of \(D_F'\). Since \(W\subset E_F'\),
it belongs to \(E_F'\). The literal identities of D.44
give \(\phi(x)=x\), \(\phi(y)=f^{-1}yf\), and
positive peripheral conjugacy at \(z\).
The image of \(f\) in \(P'\) belongs to the abelian
subgroup \(N\), which centralizes \(n_0\).
Let \(\operatorname{pr}_0:E_F\twoheadrightarrow H\)
be the identity-coordinate projection of the actual
induced image. Then
\(\xi=\operatorname{pr}_0\phi|_F:F\to H\) lies over the identity
map to \(P\). The pure rigidity just proved gives
\(\xi=\operatorname{Inn}(h)q_H\).

Write \(L=\ker q_E\), the normal core of \(\ker q_H\).
For \(w\in L\) and a coset representative \(t\),
the element \(twt^{-1}\) belongs to \(\ker q_H\).
Moreover \(\phi(t)q_E(t)^{-1}\in E_F\). Therefore
the identity-component projection of
\(q_E(t)\phi(w)q_E(t)^{-1}\) is a conjugate of
\(\xi(twt^{-1})=1\).
All six components of \(\phi(w)\) vanish, proving
\[
                L\subset\ker\phi.
 \tag{D.46.13}
\]
Thus every normalized solution factors through this
same \(E\), and is an automorphism because it is onto.
Conjugating back by \(W\) proves the assertion for the
whole peripheral fibre as well.

\paragraph{The old map and the exact common source.}
The source \(q_D\) kills \(K\), by
\textup{(D.46.6)} in every coordinate, so \(\Gamma\to D\)
is an actual epimorphism. A D.44 normalized automorphism
\(\alpha\) of \(\Gamma\) induces the identity on
the identity-component quotient \(P\): its action is
\(x\mapsto x,y\mapsto f^{-1}yf\), and the image of
\(f\in F'\) lies in \(P'\subset N\), centralizing
\(n_0\). It therefore preserves \(\ker q_P\) and
its six-coset normal core, inducing an actual
\(\alpha_D\in\operatorname{Aut}(D)\).

Residuals commute with continuous epimorphisms, by the
exact proof D.43.7. Thus the projection of \(q_E(K)\)
to the identity component is
\(O^p(O^\ell(H))=V\).
On the other hand \(q_E(K)\subset W\), since
\(D\) is a quotient of \(\Gamma\).
It is a nonzero \(D\)-submodule of the irreducible
\(W\), so
\[
                         q_E(K)=W.
 \tag{D.46.14}
\]
The actual source image in \(\Gamma\times E\)
therefore contains the entire kernel \(1\times W\)
and projects onto \(\Gamma\). This proves
\textup{(D.46.4)} and identifies \(D\) as the full
common quotient for these two source maps.

Each of the \(\ell^{\ell a}\) normalized
automorphisms \(\beta\) of \(E\) over
\(\alpha_D\) gives the automorphism
\[
               (g,e)\longmapsto(\alpha(g),\beta(e))
                   \quad\hbox{of }\Gamma\times_D E.
 \tag{D.46.15}
\]
Its source map generates the whole fibre product.
For prescribed old peripheral conjugators, choose the
upper conjugators with their matching \(D\)-images,
which is permitted by the complete fixed-conjugator
calculation above; their pairs are actual conjugators
in \(J\). Also \([J_F,W]=W\) makes
\(J_F^{\rm ab}\to\Gamma_F^{\rm ab}\) an isomorphism.
Thus \(s\sigma(s)\) lies in \(J_F'\) and projects
to the literal old conjugator. Conversely every
normalized peripheral source map to \(J\) above
the specified \(\alpha\) gives one of the just
classified maps to \(E\); \textup{(D.46.13)}
then proves that it is exactly a map
\textup{(D.46.15)}. This proves the full fibre count,
including source generation and factorization.

The source kernel in \textup{(D.46.4)} contains
\(O^\ell(K)\), because its quotient on \(K\)
is the elementary abelian \(\ell\)-group \(W\).
It is strictly smaller than \(K\), by
\textup{(D.46.14)}. The claimed strict return comparison
is therefore the actual quotient diagram
\[
 \widehat B/O^\ell(K)\twoheadrightarrow J
       \twoheadrightarrow\Gamma,
 \qquad \ker(J\to\Gamma)=W\ne1.
 \tag{D.46.16}
\]
Its pure source kernel is contained in \(O^\ell(F)\),
so the original \(P_\ell\) is a quotient of \(J_F\).
Every finite \(\ell\)-quotient of \(J_F\), composed
with \(F\to J_F\), factors through that same
\(P_\ell\). This proves its asserted maximal
pro-\(\ell\) property even though the new kernel
itself is an \(\ell\)-group.

Finally, for each of the normalized conjugator images
\(f_J\in J_F'\), choose one preimage
\(\widetilde f\in F'\). Its entire word fibre is
\[
       \widetilde f\,
         \ker\bigl(F'\longrightarrow J_F'\bigr).
 \tag{D.46.17}
\]
The epimorphism on closed commutator groups follows from
the actual epimorphism \(F\to J_F\).
This states the word-to-image map separately from the
finite number of image parameters.
